messages:
maria: Quick question — we hit another infra-only config change (log level tweak + nginx header). Should this be a patch bump (x.y.Z) or can we avoid touching semver and just use a buildmeta tag?
liam: Depends on compat surface. If behavior/API doesn't change, we usually patch. But we've been doing buildmeta for purely internal ops deltas.
anita: FWIW our deploybot currently enforces a patch bump for anything that triggers a deploy window. It was to keep releases auditable.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: detected PR #4892 merged into main; no code changes; files changed: conf/nginx.conf, infra/logging.yml; suggested tag: v1.12.4+meta.20260315 (no semver bump).
maria: @deploy-bot that's the heart of it — I like the lighter touch but worried leads/customer-facing teams may expect a semantic increment for any deploy.
jun: Can we have a rule: if only non-runtime config (comments, log levels, header ordering) => buildmeta; if anything that can change responses or SDK behavior => patch.
kai: +1. Also add an explicit opt-out label: `release/force-patch` if product wants a visible bump.
beth: What about pinning? Releases that are buildmeta-only — should downstream CI pin to the last semver or include buildmeta? Pinning to semver without buildmeta hides exact artifact.
liam: We should encourage pipelines to pin full artifact digests, but for human-facing release notes, only semver is shown. That way you can have v1.12.3 in UI but the artifact is v1.12.3+meta.20260315+sha.
anita: Rollback policy question: if we deploy a buildmeta-only change and need to roll back, do we revert to previous buildmeta or do we prefer a redeploy of the last plain semver build?
maria: Practically: redeploy previous artifact (with its exact buildmeta/sha). But to make ops easier, the console should show a “revert to previous artifact” button — not just “roll to v1.12.3”.
jun: Agree. Also propose we add a guard in deploybot: if change is config-only and deployed during a change window, allow auto-deploy; if outside window, require `release/force-out-of-window` label and a runbook link.
kai: For tagging convention suggestion: `v{MAJOR}.{MINOR}.{PATCH}+meta.{yyyymmdd}.{reason}.{gitshort}` e.g., `v1.12.4+meta.20260315.nginxhdr.a1b2c3`. Keeps machine + human readable.
beth: Love that. Add reason abbreviations doc somewhere.
liam: One more edge: database migration flags. Those are config but can alter data shape — must be patch or minor depending. Add a rule: migrations never use buildmeta.
maria: Good call. So summary proposal: 1) Default for infra-only/runtime-agnostic config — use buildmeta tag, no semver bump. 2) Any functional or data-affecting change => patch/minor as appropriate. 3) Deploybot will suggest tag and block deploys outside change window unless labeled. 4) UI will expose artifact-level revert. 5) Use tagging format from @kai.
anita: I'll update the releasebot rules and add a short PR template check to auto-detect config-only diffs and attach suggested tag.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rule update queued — will start enforcing suggested tags after tomorrow's 08:00 UTC rollout.
maria: Thanks everyone. @beth can you draft a tiny ops note for the runbook on rollback steps and reasons abbreviations?
beth: On it — will post a short doc and link in this thread. :memo:
liam: If no objections, I'll merge the deploybot config change after the canary tomorrow. Please poke if you want to test earlier.
maria: No objections from me. Going to add `release/force-patch` to the checklist for product requests.
jun: Also ping infra on the revert UI ticket, we should prioritize that before we flip enforcement.
kai: I'll add the reason abbreviations list in the infra-docs repo and link it in PR template.
beth: Done — PR 821 opened with runbook snippet.
liam: Great. Closing loop — canary tomorrow 09:30 UTC.
